title: Crimes Amendment (Mandatory Minimum Sentences for Child Sexual Abuse) Bill 2025
short_title: Crimes Amendment (Mandatory Minimum Sentences for Child Sexual Abuse) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the bill text as introduced; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend federal sentencing law to add and increase mandatory minimum prison terms for specified offences and restrict recognizance release orders.
It would insert new minimum terms into one sentencing table and lengthen existing terms in another, while requiring exceptional circumstances for specified release orders.
The release restrictions would apply to sentences for Commonwealth child sex offences, and the bill would commence on the day following Royal Assent.
changes: Six listed Criminal Code offences would receive minimum prison terms of five years.
Six listed terms in subsection 16AAB(2) would increase from four years to six years.
Courts would need exceptional circumstances to justify making either an initial or a new recognizance release order for a Commonwealth child sex offence.
summary.affected: Courts sentencing people for the listed offences and people sentenced for Commonwealth child sex offences are affected.
